events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.68)
events.body:
The dispute is a rider-side no-show fee challenge: the driver cancelled at 09:59:25 and Ryde charged the published $6.61 [F4][F8]. Under NS-0, a driver cancellation relying on rider no-show is routed through NS-1/NS-2 [F4][NS-0].

NS-1 is conjunctive. Element (ii) is satisfied: the driver first came within 200 m of the pickup at 09:54:55, was 38 m away at closest approach, and was 40 m away at the moment of the tap [F1][F2][F6][NS-1]. Element (iii) is satisfied: he stayed within 200 m for 3 min 5 s after the tap and was stationary 38 m from the pickup for 3 min 25 s before cancelling, both above the >180 s threshold [F3][F6][NS-1].

Element (i) turns on the internal conflict in the same timeline source: F6 records an "I'm Here" tap at 09:56:20, while F7 records the tap field as null [F6][F7]. The system-record preference rule does not break this tie, because both entries are timeline records of the same system; what it does resolve is the conflict between the driver's statement and chat (F10, F11, F12) and the timeline, and the contemporaneous chat announcement of presence at 09:56 corroborates the tap timestamp [F10][F11][F12][NS-1]. The more specific entry — an exact timestamp and distance (09:56:20, 40 m) — outweighs a null field, and the platform's own arrival recording at 09:54:55 with cancellation 4 min 30 s later shows the wait NS-1 protects actually occurred [F5][F6][NS-1].

On that basis the no-show branch is properly applied and the fee stands, so no refund arises under NS-2 [F8][F4][NS-2]. No separate overcharge exists: the fee is the published $6.61 with a 1.0× multiplier, so FARE-1 adds nothing to refund [F8][F9][FARE-1]. The rider's own timing account ("a minute after") is a statement with no system record behind it, and profiles on both sides (F16, F17) cannot decide the merits [F16][F17][NS-1]. No account flag is imposed: the record shows genuine proximity and waiting rather than abuse of the arrival or waiting button, and no clause conditions a flag here [F2][F3][NS-2].

ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $6.61 cancellation fee; do not refund; note the F6/F7 timeline conflict for data-quality review.

what_would_change: Had the driver tapped I'm Here more than 200 m away, or left before 3 minutes, NS-2 would refund the fee in full.

claims.assertion: NS-1 requires the driver to have pressed "I'm Here" as a precondition of the passenger no-show fee, but the timeline record shows the driver never pressed it (driver_pressed_here_at is null), so the $6.61 fee fails NS-1(i).
The driver's written statement and chat claim he "pressed I'm Here" (F12, F11), but the system timeline contradicts this (F7); the system record wins, so the no-show fee cannot stand.
The $6.61 cancellation fee was charged under the rider-no-show branch while the driver cancelled without satisfying NS-1, so under NS-2 it must be refunded in full.

The driver was within 200 m of the pickup for 4 min 30 s before cancelling (first within 200 m at 09:54:55, cancelled 09:59:25) and stationary 38 m away for 3 min 25 s — but proximity alone does not cure the missing "I'm Here" tap required by NS-1(i).

The rider's own report that she came out a minute after the cancellation is consistent with the driver cancelling at 09:59:25 rather than continuing to wait, and nothing in the record shows the rider was contacted or given a further chance before the driver cancelled.

weaknesses: F6 shows a "I'm Here" tap at 09:56:20, 40 m from pickup, with 3 min 5 s inside 200 m afterwards — the other side will rely on F6 plus F5 (platform-recorded arrival 09:54:55) and F3 (stationary 3 min 25 s at 38 m) to argue NS-1 was in substance satisfied. My case turns on the conflict between F6 and F7 in the same timeline source.

F2 and F3 show the driver genuinely did wait in excess of three minutes within 200 m, so the rider's lateness is real and the driver's narrative in F12/F10/F11 (chat 09:56 "I'm here", 09:59 "Waited more than 3 min, cancelling") is not absurd.
The rider's profile (F16) shows 3 disputes in 90 days with 2 no-show disputes upheld, which the other side may use to suggest a pattern of claiming no-shows.
The rider offered no chat message or other evidence that she responded to the driver at the pickup point; the only support for her timing is her own complaint, which no system record confirms.

claims.assertion: The driver's GPS position satisfied the 'at the pick-up location' requirement: his closest approach to the pickup point was 38 m at 09:58:25 and he first came within 200 m at 09:54:55, remaining inside that radius for a cumulative 4 min 30 s before cancelling — well inside the 200 m arrival radius used for NS-1(ii).

The driver waited at the pickup point for more than 3 minutes: he was stationary at coordinates 38 m from the pickup from 09:56:00 until the 09:59:25 cancellation, i.e. 3 min 25 s of stationary waiting, and total time within 200 m was 4 min 30 s — both exceed the >180 s (≥3:01) threshold in NS-1(iii).

The platform's own timeline records driver arrival at the pickup at 09:54:55 and the cancellation 4 min 30 s later, confirming the wait exceeded the 3-minute minimum required before a no-show cancellation may be charged.

The driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 09:56:20 while 40 m from the pickup point and stayed within 200 m for 3 min 5 s after the tap, satisfying NS-1(i) as corroborated by the chat message 'I'm here at the pickup point, black Hyundai Ioniq' sent at 09:56.

All three NS-1 conditions (tap, GPS within the pickup radius, wait over 3 minutes) are met, so the $6.61 rider cancellation fee stands in full and the rider's request for a refund should be refused: no_action, with no refund computable from F8.
No surcharge manipulation is present: the cancellation fee on record is the published $6.61 with a 1.0x surge multiplier, so there is no overcharge component to refund under the fare rules either.

The surrounding road conditions were normal (no traffic incidents near the route, band 3 speed 20-29 km/h, fair weather 0.0 mm rain), so there is no extraneous circumstance suggesting the wait or cancellation was anything other than a genuine rider no-show.

The rider's own 90-day record shows 3 disputes with 2 upheld no-show claims while the driver has 645 trips in 90 days and 0 disputes upheld; this pattern supports upholding the driver's no-show action without any account flag against the driver.

weaknesses: The timeline contains a contradictory entry: F7 states the driver never tapped 'I'm Here' (driver_pressed_here_at is null), which directly conflicts with F6 (tap at 09:56:20) and the driver's own statement in F12 — the rider will rely on F7 to argue NS-1(i) fails and that the fee must be refunded under NS-2.

The rider's complaint says they came out 'a minute after the driver cancelled' (F8/F4 context, cancellation 09:59:25); if accepted, this supports their position that they were about to arrive, though the 4 min 30 s recorded within 200 m (F2, F5) shows the driver's wait already exceeded the policy minimum before cancelling.

The extra 40 s of wait beyond the 3-minute minimum is thin, so the rider may argue the driver cancelled hastily; NS-1 imposes no longer grace period beyond the 3:01 requirement, but a human reviewer could still view the timing as harsh.

The rider's profile (F16) shows 2 of 3 prior disputes upheld in their favour on no-show issues, which the rider may use to suggest their account is credible, though profile facts cannot decide the case.

points.response: Conceded as far as GPS goes — F1 (closest approach 38 m) and F2 (first within 200 m at 09:54:55, 4 min 30 s inside) do establish NS-1(ii) — but NS-1 is conjunctive and (ii) alone cannot carry the fee.
Conceded on duration: F3 (stationary 09:56:00–09:59:25) and F2 give 3 min 25 s stationary and 4 min 30 s inside 200 m, satisfying NS-1(iii); this does not save the fee because NS-1(i) is still unmet.

F5 records arrival and the interval to cancellation but says nothing about the "I'm Here" tap, which is the separate NS-1(i) precondition; NS-1 requires all of (i), (ii) and (iii), not a mere elapsed wait.

F6 and F7 are two entries in the same timeline source and directly contradict each other on the tap; where a chat statement (F10, F12) and the system record conflict the system record wins, and the driver's narrative must not be used to resolve the contradiction in his own favour.
The premise of D5 fails: with NS-1(i) unproven the no-show branch does not close, so NS-2 applies and the $6.61 recorded in F8 must be refunded in full via refund_full.

This is not an overcharge case under FARE-1 — the fee is the published $6.61 (F8, F9) — the rider's objection is that the NS-1 preconditions for charging it were never met, which NS-2 resolves regardless of the amount.
Fair weather and normal traffic (F13, F14, F15) are irrelevant to NS-1, which conditions the fee on the tap, the GPS radius and the wait — not on road conditions.

Profile facts cannot decide the merits, and F16 actually cuts against the driver's narrative: the rider's two prior no-show disputes were upheld in the rider's favour, while F17 shows the driver's history is silent on tap-button conduct — no flag is sought against the driver in this case.

The rider's case rests on a single null field in F7 while the same timeline source records the tap in F6 ('I'm Here' at 09:56:20, 40 m from pickup, 3 min 5 s within 200 m afterwards); the rider cannot pick one timeline entry (F7) and discard the other (F6) from the same source, and the tap is independently corroborated by the driver's chat at 09:56 (F10) and by F5 (platform-recorded arrival 09:54:55).

F7 does not contradict F6/F10/F12 in the way claimed — it is the rider who asks the judge to treat a chat statement as beating a system record, but the system records (F5 arrival at 09:54:55, F2 cumulative 4 min 30 s within 200 m, F3 stationary 3 min 25 s at 38 m) all confirm the physical facts NS-1 protects, namely the driver being at the pickup point and waiting over three minutes.

NS-2 only returns the $6.61 if any of NS-1(i)(ii)(iii) fails, and here all three are met on the recorded evidence (tap F6, GPS inside the pickup radius F1/F2, wait over 3 minutes F3/F5), so the no-show branch under NS-0 is properly applied and no refund is due.

The rider concedes proximity and a 3 min 25 s stationery wait (F2, F3) but argues the tap is what fails; that argument collapses because F6 records the tap at 09:56:20, 3 min 5 s before the 09:59:25 cancellation (F4), which is exactly the ordering NS-1(i) and (iii) require.

The rider's timing ('a minute after') is a statement in the complaint with no system record behind it, while the timeline shows the driver was inside 200 m from 09:54:55 and waited 4 min 30 s cumulatively (F5, F2), and the driver's messages show he announced his presence at 09:56 before cancelling at 09:59 (F10, F11); NS-1 sets the wait at just over 3 minutes and does not require the driver to keep waiting indefinitely.

I acknowledge the internal tension between F7 and F6 in the timeline slice; even so, F6 is specific as to time and distance (09:56:20, 40 m) and is corroborated by the driver's contemporaneous chat (F10), so the more detailed record controls and NS-1(i) is satisfied.
